title: Electrolysis of Aqueous Solutions - Worksheet 2
topic: Electrolysis of Concentrated and Dilute Aqueous Solutions
subject: Pure Chemistry

questions.question: What is observed at the cathode during electrolysis of concentrated sodium chloride solution using inert electrodes?
options: Silvery metal deposits on the electrode
Pinkish metal deposits on the electrode
Bubbles of greenish-yellow gas with choking smell
Bubbles of colourless gas that burns with a pop
questions.explanation: In concentrated NaCl solution, H⁺ ions from water are preferentially discharged over Na⁺ ions at the cathode: 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂. Hydrogen gas burns with a pop sound.

questions.question: Which half-equation represents the reaction at the anode during electrolysis of dilute sulfuric acid using platinum electrodes?
options: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻
2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂
4OH⁻ → O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e⁻
SO₄²⁻ → SO₄ + 2e⁻
questions.explanation: In dilute H₂SO₄, OH⁻ ions from water are preferentially discharged over SO₄²⁻ ions at the anode: 4OH⁻ → O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e⁻, producing oxygen gas.

questions.question: Why is hydrogen produced instead of sodium at the cathode during electrolysis of aqueous sodium chloride?
options: Sodium ions are too large to reach the cathode
Hydrogen is lower than sodium in the reactivity series
Water molecules block sodium ions from the cathode
Hydrogen ions are more concentrated than sodium ions
questions.explanation: In aqueous solutions, the ion lower in the reactivity series is preferentially discharged. Since hydrogen is below sodium, H⁺ ions are reduced to H₂ instead of Na⁺ to Na.

questions.question: What is observed when concentrated copper(II) sulfate solution is electrolysed using copper electrodes?
options: Gas bubbles at both electrodes
Cathode increases in mass, anode decreases in mass
Blue solution fades at both electrodes
Both electrodes increase in mass
questions.explanation: With copper electrodes in CuSO₄ solution: Cathode: Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu (copper deposits, mass increases). Anode: Cu → Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ (copper dissolves, mass decreases). This is electrorefining.

questions.question: During electrolysis of dilute sodium chloride solution, what is the product at the anode?
options: Chlorine gas
Hydrogen gas
Sodium metal
Oxygen gas
questions.explanation: In dilute NaCl solution, OH⁻ ions are preferentially discharged over Cl⁻ ions at the anode: 4OH⁻ → O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e⁻, producing oxygen gas. Concentration affects preferential discharge.

questions.question: How does the pH of the solution change during electrolysis of concentrated sodium chloride solution?
options: pH remains constant throughout the solution
pH decreases at both electrodes
pH increases at the cathode, decreases at the anode
pH decreases at the cathode, increases at the anode
questions.explanation: At cathode: H⁺ discharged, leaving OH⁻ behind → pH increases (alkaline). At anode: Cl⁻ discharged to Cl₂, but OH⁻ also consumed → pH may decrease slightly. Overall, solution near cathode becomes alkaline.

questions.question: Which product is obtained at the cathode during electrolysis of dilute copper(II) sulfate using inert electrodes?
options: Sulfuric acid forms at the cathode
Oxygen gas is produced at the cathode
Copper metal deposits as a pinkish-brown layer
Hydrogen gas bubbles form on the electrode
questions.explanation: In dilute CuSO₄, Cu²⁺ ions are preferentially discharged over H⁺ ions at the cathode because copper is lower than hydrogen in the electrochemical series: Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu.

questions.question: What happens to the concentration of copper(II) sulfate solution during electrolysis using inert electrodes?
options: Concentration first increases then decreases
Concentration decreases as copper ions are removed
Concentration remains constant throughout
Concentration increases as water is electrolysed
questions.explanation: With inert electrodes, Cu²⁺ ions are removed at the cathode (Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu) but not replaced at the anode (where OH⁻ → O₂). Therefore, Cu²⁺ concentration decreases, and the blue colour fades.

questions.question: Why does the blue colour of copper(II) sulfate solution fade during electrolysis with inert electrodes?
options: Water molecules dilute the copper ion concentration
Sulfate ions are discharged to form sulfur
Copper ions are oxidised to copper(III) ions
Copper ions are reduced and deposited as metal
questions.explanation: The blue colour is due to Cu²⁺(aq) ions. During electrolysis with inert electrodes, Cu²⁺ ions are reduced at the cathode to copper metal and removed from solution, causing the colour to fade.

questions.question: During electrolysis of aqueous sodium sulfate using inert electrodes, what gases are produced?
options: Chlorine at anode, hydrogen at cathode
No gases; only metals are deposited
Hydrogen at cathode, oxygen at anode
Oxygen at cathode, hydrogen at anode
questions.explanation: In aqueous Na₂SO₄, the ions are Na⁺, SO₄²⁻, H⁺, OH⁻. At cathode: H⁺ reduced to H₂. At anode: OH⁻ oxidised to O₂. Na⁺ and SO₄²⁻ remain in solution.

questions.question: How does the pH change during electrolysis of aqueous sodium sulfate?
options: pH becomes acidic at both electrodes
pH remains neutral throughout the solution
pH increases at cathode, decreases at anode
pH decreases at cathode, increases at anode
questions.explanation: At cathode: H⁺ discharged, leaving OH⁻ → pH increases (alkaline). At anode: OH⁻ discharged, leaving H⁺ → pH decreases (acidic). The solution becomes locally alkaline at cathode, acidic at anode.

questions.question: What is the main application of electrolysis of concentrated brine (aqueous NaCl)?
options: Generation of electricity from salt water
Production of chlorine, hydrogen, and sodium hydroxide
Purification of salt for food consumption
Extraction of sodium metal for industrial use
questions.explanation: The chlor-alkali industry electrolyses concentrated brine to produce: Cl₂ (anode) for disinfectants/PVC, H₂ (cathode) for ammonia/fuel, and NaOH (in solution) for soap/paper.

questions.question: During electrolysis of aqueous silver nitrate using inert electrodes, what is deposited at the cathode?
options: Oxygen gas displaces silver from solution
Nitrogen gas is produced at the cathode
Hydrogen gas bubbles form on the electrode
Silver metal as a shiny grey deposit
questions.explanation: Ag⁺ is much lower than H⁺ in the reactivity series, so Ag⁺ is preferentially reduced: Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag. Silver metal deposits as a shiny grey layer on the cathode.

questions.question: Why does the pH of the solution increase near the cathode during electrolysis of aqueous potassium nitrate?
options: Water molecules split to produce hydroxide ions
Nitrate ions migrate to the cathode and form base
Hydrogen ions are discharged, leaving hydroxide ions
Potassium ions are reduced to form KOH
questions.explanation: At the cathode, H⁺ ions from water are discharged: 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂. This removes H⁺, leaving excess OH⁻ ions behind, making the solution near the cathode alkaline (pH increases).

questions.question: Which statement correctly explains why chlorine is produced at the anode in concentrated NaCl but oxygen in dilute NaCl?
options: Concentrated solutions have lower activation energy for Cl⁻ oxidation
Higher Cl⁻ concentration favours Cl⁻ discharge over OH⁻ discharge
Dilute solutions contain more oxygen molecules to discharge
Chloride ions are larger and move faster in concentrated solutions
questions.explanation: Preferential discharge depends on ion concentration. In concentrated NaCl, high [Cl⁻] favours Cl⁻ → Cl₂. In dilute NaCl, low [Cl⁻] allows OH⁻ → O₂ to dominate, even though OH⁻ is harder to oxidise.

questions.question: During electrolysis of aqueous copper(II) chloride using inert electrodes, what gases are produced?
options: No gases; only metals are deposited
Oxygen at anode, copper at cathode
Chlorine at cathode, hydrogen at anode
Hydrogen at cathode, chlorine at anode
questions.explanation: In aqueous CuCl₂: At cathode, Cu²⁺ is reduced to Cu (not H₂, as Cu is below H). At anode, Cl⁻ is oxidised to Cl₂ (Cl⁻ concentration is high). So: Cu deposits, Cl₂ gas evolves.

questions.question: What happens to the mass of the anode during electrolysis of aqueous copper(II) sulfate using copper electrodes?
options: Mass fluctuates as copper dissolves and redeposits
Mass decreases as copper atoms dissolve from it
Mass remains constant as no reaction occurs
Mass increases as copper ions deposit on it
questions.explanation: With copper anode: Cu → Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻. Copper atoms from the anode dissolve into solution as Cu²⁺ ions, causing the anode to lose mass. This is used in electrorefining of copper.

questions.question: Why is platinum or graphite preferred over reactive metals as electrodes in aqueous electrolysis?
options: They increase the voltage of the electrolytic cell
They are cheaper and easier to obtain
They do not react with the electrolyte or products
They conduct electricity more efficiently
questions.explanation: Inert electrodes like platinum or graphite do not participate in the electrolysis reactions. Reactive metal electrodes might dissolve or react with products, interfering with the intended electrolysis.

questions.question: During electrolysis of aqueous sodium hydroxide using inert electrodes, what is the overall effect on the solution?
options: No change; only water is electrolysed
Sodium hydroxide concentration decreases
Water is decomposed; NaOH concentration increases
Sodium hydroxide concentration increases
questions.explanation: In aqueous NaOH, water is electrolysed: 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂. Na⁺ and OH⁻ are spectator ions. As water is removed, the concentration of NaOH in the remaining solution increases.

questions.question: Which factor determines whether hydrogen or a metal is produced at the cathode in aqueous electrolysis?
options: The surface area of the cathode electrode
The position of the metal in the reactivity series
The temperature of the electrolytic cell
The concentration of the metal ion in solution
questions.explanation: The key factor is the reactivity series. Metals above hydrogen (e.g., Na, K, Ca) are more reactive; H⁺ is preferentially reduced. Metals below hydrogen (e.g., Cu, Ag) are less reactive; metal ions are reduced.
